raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add `--profile-dir` to `vllm bench forward` (#61339): a per-kernel GPU time breakdown of each benchmarked batch, in a form an agent or a script can read and compare directly.

## Claims

- `--profile-dir DIR`: after timing, each case's graph is replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`. Every rank writes `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (Perfetto) and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted, with call counts and one full name per group). Rank 0's top kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
- Only the timed forward is counted: the in-graph KV restore and rank rendezvous that precede it in each replay are left out (reported as `pre_forward_us`), so the profile accounts for the same interval as `median_us`.
- `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]` prints one summary, or a per-kernel diff of two (e.g. before/after a change) sorted by the largest change.
- Nsight Systems: each case's 3 profiled replays always run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat --cuda-graph-trace=node` records just them, one small report per case (and per rank with `torchrun --no-python nsys ...`). `--profile-dir` and nsys can't share CUPTI; combining them fails with a clear message.
- Timing runs before profiling, so reported latencies are unchanged; without a profiler the extra 3 replays per case are the only cost.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 4 passed (GB200): new summary unit test; the end-to-end test now also runs --profile-dir
```

Llama-3.2-1B, 1 GPU: profiled forward span vs timed median: decode 1291 vs 1265 us, prefill 4755 vs 4498 us, prefix hit 1782 vs 1770 us (profiler overhead; prefill's own sample spread was 1.75%). Decode excluded 512 restore copies per replay (~830 us), as intended.

Nsight Systems (2025.5), Llama-3.2-1B: one ~680 KB report per case; `nsys stats --report nvtx_sum` shows the `forward/<case>` range and `cuda_gpu_kern_sum` matches the JSON summary (48 calls = 16 layers x 3 replays). DP2 via `torchrun --no-python nsys`: one report per rank per case. `--profile-dir` under nsys: fails with the CUPTI message.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (1 GB200 node), ~100K KV: all 4 ranks wrote traces and summaries; span vs median: decode b32 15731 vs 15734 us, b128 20087 vs 19975 us, prefill 16K 204.2 vs ~202 ms. Example (prefill 16K, rank 0):

```
        us      %  calls  kernel
   62146.8  30.35     40  deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl
   22000.9  10.74    131  kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinfergemmkernelsdense_blockscaled_gemm_sm100Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel
   20274.8   9.90     40  fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H512PagedKvDenseDynamicTokenSparseP1VarSeqQ64Kv128PersistentKeepsAbForGen
   19139.9   9.35      2  _engram_lookup_kernel
   10378.6   5.07     23  vllm::topKPerRowPrefill
```

## Details

- Each replay's GPU activities are split into the `len(state_views)` restore copies (one copy each), the rendezvous all-reduce (multi-rank), and the forward. The summary checks that the activities divide evenly into replays and raises otherwise.
- Kernel names are grouped without return type, template and function arguments (`void ns::foo<T>(...)` -> `ns::foo`); generic launchers keep their first template argument (`cutlass::device_kernel<Op>`), CuTe DSL names drop their per-shape suffix. Non-kernel activities (memcpy/memset) keep their names.
- `span_us` is first-to-last forward activity and should track `median_us`; `busy_us` sums kernel durations and can exceed it with multi-stream overlap.
- Why both: `torch.profiler` needs no extra tooling, is scoped per case in-process, and is tested in CI, so it backs the agent-facing JSON summary and diff. Nsight Systems adds NVTX, NCCL, CPU-side and GPU-metric views that many users reach for; the capture range makes it record only the benchmarked replays instead of the whole process (load, JIT, warmup, timing).
- The model-microbenchmark skill gets a short "Kernel breakdown" section on both workflows (including keeping `--capture-range-end=repeat`, since nsys's default stops after the first case and leaves the bench hanging).
- Size: `profile.py` ~200 lines plus ~40 lines of wiring; tests and docs ~60.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GPU kernel profiles of `vllm bench forward` cases.
+
+With `--profile-dir`, each case's graph is replayed a few more times under
+`torch.profiler` after timing. Each rank writes a Perfetto trace and a kernel
+summary (`<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json`): per-kernel time per forward, sorted.
+
+Summarize one file or compare two (e.g. before/after a change):
+`python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]`.
+
+The same replays run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range per
+case (with or without `--profile-dir`), so Nsight Systems can record just them:
+`nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat
+--cuda-graph-trace=node vllm bench forward ...`.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import json
+import statistics
+from collections import defaultdict
+from typing import Any
+
+import regex as re
+import torch
+
+_GPU_CATEGORIES = ("kernel", "gpu_memcpy", "gpu_memset")
+# Kernels named after a generic launcher are identified by their first
+# template argument instead.
+_GENERIC = re.compile(r"(^|::)(device_kernel|Kernel|kernel|KernelWrapper)$")
+# CuTe DSL kernel names embed per-shape layouts after these markers.
+_CUTE_DSL_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"_object_at_|_tensorptr")
+
+
+def _match_back(text: str, end: int, open_ch: str, close_ch: str) -> int:
+    """Index of the bracket opening the one closing at `end`, skipping
+    brackets of the other kind nested inside parentheses."""
+    depth, parens = 0, 0
+    for i in range(end, -1, -1):
+        ch = text[i]
+        if open_ch == "<" and ch in "()":
+            parens += 1 if ch == ")" else -1
+            continue
+        if parens:
+            continue
+        if ch == close_ch:
+            depth += 1
+        elif ch == open_ch:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return i
+    return -1
+
+
+def short_name(name: str) -> str:
+    """`void ns::foo<T, 4>(args)` -> `ns::foo`: return type, template and
+    function arguments dropped. Generic launchers (e.g.
+    `cutlass::device_kernel<Op<...>>`) keep their first template argument."""
+    if name.startswith("kernel_cutlass_"):
+        return _CUTE_DSL_SUFFIX.split(name, maxsplit=1)[0]
+    head = name.strip()
+    if head.endswith(")"):
+        head = head[: max(_match_back(head, len(head) - 1, "(", ")"), 0)].rstrip()
+    template = ""
+    if head.endswith(">"):
+        start = _match_back(head, len(head) - 1, "<", ">")
+        if start > 0:
+            head, template = head[:start], head[start + 1 : -1]
+    base = head.split()[-1] if head.split() else name
+    if _GENERIC.search(base) and template:
+        arg = re.split(r"[<>(,]", template, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
+        if arg:
+            return f"{base}<{arg.removeprefix('void ')}>"
+    return base
+
+
+def summarize(events: list[dict], replays: int, skip: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Per-forward kernel times from the GPU activities of `replays` replays.
+
+    Each replay first runs `skip` activities that aren't part of the timed
+    forward (the KV state restore and the rank rendezvous); they are reported
+    separately as `pre_forward_us`.
+    """
+    acts = sorted(
+        (e for e in events if e.get("cat") in _GPU_CATEGORIES and "dur" in e),
+        key=lambda e: e["ts"],
+    )
+    if not acts:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "No GPU activity recorded. Another profiler (e.g. nsys) may hold "
+            "CUPTI; don't combine --profile-dir with it."
+        )
+    if len(acts) % replays:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{len(acts)} GPU activities don't split into {replays} replays"
+        )
+    per_replay = len(acts) // replays
+    if per_replay <= skip:
+        raise ValueError(f"{per_replay} activities per replay, {skip} to skip")
+    kernels: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = defaultdict(
+        lambda: {"total_us": 0.0, "calls": 0, "example": ""}
+    )
+    spans, busy, pre = [], [], []
+    for r in range(replays):
+        chunk = acts[r * per_replay : (r + 1) * per_replay]
+        pre.append(sum(e["dur"] for e in chunk[:skip]))
+        forward = chunk[skip:]
+        spans.append(
+            max(e["ts"] + e["dur"] for e in forward) - min(e["ts"] for e in forward)
+        )
+        busy.append(sum(e["dur"] for e in forward))
+        for e in forward:
+            name = short_name(e["name"]) if e["cat"] == "kernel" else e["name"]
+            k = kernels[name]
+            k["total_us"] += e["dur"]
+            k["calls"] += 1
+            k["example"] = k["example"] or e["name"][:300]
+    total = sum(k["total_us"] for k in kernels.values())
+    rows = [
+        {
+            "name": name,
+            "us": round(k["total_us"] / replays, 2),
+            "pct": round(100 * k["total_us"] / total, 2),
+            "calls": k["calls"] // replays,
+            "example": k["example"],
+        }
+        for name, k in kernels.items()
+    ]
+    rows.sort(key=lambda row: -row["us"])
+    return {
+        "replays": replays,
+        # First to last forward activity; busy can exceed it when streams overlap.
+        "span_us": round(statistics.median(spans), 2),
+        "busy_us": round(statistics.median(busy), 2),
+        "pre_forward_us": round(statistics.median(pre), 2),
+        "activities": per_replay - skip,
+        "kernels": rows,
+    }
+
+
+def profile_graph(
+    graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph,
+    name: str,
+    prefix: str | None,
+    skip: int,
+    replays: int = 3,
+) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Replay `replays` times between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop`, in an NVTX
+    range named after the case, for `nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`.
+
+    With `prefix`, also trace them with `torch.profiler` and write
+    `prefix.trace.json.gz` and `prefix.kernels.json`. Every rank must call
+    this (replays may contain collectives).
+    """
+
+    def run() -> None:
+        torch.cuda.profiler.start()
+        with torch.cuda.nvtx.range(f"forward/{name}"):
+            for _ in range(replays):
+                graph.replay()
+                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.profiler.stop()
+
+    if prefix is None:
+        run()
+        return None
+    activities = [torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]
+    with torch.profiler.profile(activities=activities) as prof:
+        run()
+    trace = f"{prefix}.trace.json.gz"
+    prof.export_chrome_trace(trace)
+    with gzip.open(trace, "rt") as f:
+        events = json.load(f)["traceEvents"]
+    summary = {"trace": trace, **summarize(events, replays, skip)}
+    with open(f"{prefix}.kernels.json", "w") as f:
+        json.dump(summary, f, indent=1)
+    return summary
+
+
+def format_summary(summary: dict[str, Any], top: int = 20) -> str:
+    lines = [
+        f"span {summary['span_us']:.1f} us, busy {summary['busy_us']:.1f} us, "
+        f"{summary['activities']} activities/forward",
+        f"{'us':>10} {'%':>6} {'calls':>6}  kernel",
+    ]
+    for row in summary["kernels"][:top]:
+        lines.append(
+            f"{row['us']:10.1f} {row['pct']:6.2f} {row['calls']:6d}  {row['name']}"
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def format_diff(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any], top: int = 20) -> str:
+    rows_a = {row["name"]: row for row in a["kernels"]}
+    rows_b = {row["name"]: row for row in b["kernels"]}
+    deltas = []
+    for name in rows_a.keys() | rows_b.keys():
+        ra, rb = rows_a.get(name), rows_b.get(name)
+        us_a, us_b = ra["us"] if ra else 0.0, rb["us"] if rb else 0.0
+        calls_a, calls_b = ra["calls"] if ra else 0, rb["calls"] if rb else 0
+        deltas.append((us_b - us_a, us_a, us_b, calls_a, calls_b, name))
+    deltas.sort(key=lambda d: -abs(d[0]))
+    lines = [
+        f"span {a['span_us']:.1f} -> {b['span_us']:.1f} us "
+        f"({b['span_us'] - a['span_us']:+.1f}), busy {a['busy_us']:.1f} -> "
+        f"{b['busy_us']:.1f} us ({b['busy_us'] - a['busy_us']:+.1f})",
+        f"{'delta us':>10} {'A us':>10} {'B us':>10} {'A n':>5} {'B n':>5}  kernel",
+    ]
+    for delta, us_a, us_b, calls_a, calls_b, name in deltas[:top]:
+        lines.append(
+            f"{delta:+10.1f} {us_a:10.1f} {us_b:10.1f} {calls_a:5d} {calls_b:5d}  "
+            f"{name}"
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("summaries", nargs="+", help="One or two *.kernels.json.")
+    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=20)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if len(args.summaries) > 2:
+        parser.error("Pass one summary, or two to compare.")
+    loaded = []
+    for path in args.summaries:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            loaded.append(json.load(f))
+    if len(loaded) == 1:
+        print(format_summary(loaded[0], args.top))
+    else:
+        print(format_diff(loaded[0], loaded[1], args.top))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
